messages:
maya (PM): Quick sync — we need to finalize the PRD acceptance criteria for embeddings/rerank changes: dim migration, normalization, and batch semantics. Customer asks are piling up.

sam (ML Eng): Agree. Main tradeoffs: backward compatibility for vectors, storage cost if we increase dim, and how normalization interacts with existing rerank model.

leo (Infra): Also need to think about how batch semantics affect request routing and KV cache invalidation. If we change semantics mid-rollout, cache hits drop.

anya (SWE): Draft acceptance criteria suggestion: 1) No user-visible drop in rerank precision > 1% on canaries, 2) zero downtime migration path for dim changes (fallback to old model), 3) batch API remains stable for concurrent requests.

oliver (Support): Real customer asks: ACME wants 1536 -> 2048 dim with exact similarity parity to previous results for top-5. They need audit logs showing rollout window.

maya (PM): Good. Also include: explicit perf targets (median latency <= 120ms on Dedicated small), and rollout gates (quality, latency, infra).

sam (ML Eng): Edge cases we must call out in PRD: - mixed-dim queries (client sends old dims), - normalization mismatch (L2 vs. cosine pre/post normalization), - batch reorder vs. prefix-caching.

anya (SWE): For mixed-dim queries propose server-side rejection with clear error code + migration flag for clients. Alternative: autoscale a conversion path (costly). Which is acceptable?

maya (PM): Prioritize server-side reject + migration docs for GA. Conversion path as a post-GA feature if customers sign up. Put conversion as P2.

leo (Infra): Regarding batch semantics: if we introduce per-request normalization we must ensure batching doesn't mix normalization contexts. Implementation note: attach 'norm_version' to batched request meta so runtime can split batches. That keeps latency gains.

sam (ML Eng): Good idea. Acceptance test: synthetic load with mixed norm_version values must preserve per-request normalization and not regress throughput by >10%.

oliver (Support): Also need clear error message text: `400: embedding-dimension-mismatch — expected 1536, got 1024. See migration guide: <link>`

maya (PM): Launch checklist items: - Docs + migration guide, - Canary test with top-5 parity metric, - Rollout policy with automatic fallback, - Support playbook. Assign owners.

anya (SWE): Owner: me for API + error surfaces. Sam for model validation and parity tests. Leo for runtime routing & batching changes. Maya for docs and rollout plan. Oliver for customer comms.

sam (ML Eng): For parity tests I’ll create an eval harness: run on ACME sample set and compute top-k consistency and rerank NDCG difference. Criteria: NDCG_drop <= 0.01 and top-5 intersection >= 0.9.

leo (Infra): Can we quantify cache invalidation impact? Proposal: prefix cache keys include (model_version, dim, norm_version). We accept short-term hit during canary but must monitor cache miss spike < 2x baseline.

maya (PM): Add monitoring requirements: token-level cost, cache-miss rate, latency p50/p95, and rerank-quality regression alerts. Also a scheduled rollback window of 30 minutes per canary.

oliver (Support): I'll draft the customer-facing communication template and the audit log format: include timestamp, from_dim, to_dim, model_version, canary_percent.

sam (ML Eng): Edge-case: embeddings generated with per-customer normalization toggles. We'll need to preserve per-customer metadata and make the runtime consult customer config. Add that to PRD.

anya (SWE): API schema patch: add optional `embedding_meta` object with `dim` and `norm_version` fields. Backward compatible since it's optional. We'll return explicit error if mismatch.

maya (PM): OK. Acceptance criteria (final): 1) Quality parity gates as Sam specified, 2) No-regression latency p95 <= baseline + 30ms on Dedicated small, 3) Error path for mixed-dim with clear docs, 4) Batching respects norm_version and throughput regression <= 10%, 5) Monitoring & rollback in place.

leo (Infra): Timeline concern: infra changes (batch split by norm_version) will take ~2 sprints. Do we want to scope to allow simple reject + docs first, then batching improvements later?

maya (PM): Yes. Scope negotiation: GA v1 = reject-mixed-dim + per-request norm_version support + docs + canary. GA v2 = conversion path + batching split + autop-run conversions. We’ll aim for v1 in 6 weeks.

oliver (Support): Customer success ask: offer migration assistance for large accounts (manual conversion). Mark as P1 for enterprise customers.

sam (ML Eng): I'll prepare a lightweight conversion script for teams to try manually; mark as experimental.

anya (SWE): One more edge: embeddings in storage (replay/legacy). Need a migration tool to re-embed historical vectors or attach `dim` metadata so reranker can detect and handle them. Add to backlog.

maya (PM): Noted. I'll update PRD draft with these sections and ping for RFC review tomorrow. Quick decisions logged: server-side reject for mixed-dim (P0 for GA v1), norm_version attached to batch metadata (P0), conversion path (P2 post-GA), batch-split infra (P1 post-GA).

ci-bot: Deploy scheduled: updated PRD draft pushed to `eng-ml/prd/embeddings-norm-batch.md` (link).

maya (PM): Thanks everyone — please add any final comments inline in the PRD doc; we'll lock acceptance criteria by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
